Spotlight: Not beaten far in good-quality 7f races on first two starts, shaping with significant promise before fading into midfield in valuable Glorious Goodwood maiden (good to firm) on latter occasion; drops in trip here; must be considered.

RaceName: Moloney's Bar And Music Venue Maiden
Spotlight: Out the back in a bumper in May; will need more experience.

RaceName: Moloney's Bar And Music Venue Maiden
Spotlight: 100-1, missed the break when beaten 12l over a mile at Naas.

RaceName: Moloney's Bar And Music Venue Maiden
Spotlight: Beaten a long way at Fairyhouse; gelded.

RaceName: Moloney's Bar And Music Venue Maiden
OwnerName: Exors Of The Late H H Aga Khan
Spotlight: A place ahead of smart Enceladus when second at Naas last year; off the bridle a long way out when second on his return at Leopardstown (1m1f), and not mad about his head carriage that day.

RaceName: Moloney's Bar And Music Venue Maiden
Spotlight: Prominent racer has put in three solid efforts; led when third at Leopardstown, little over a length behind Handani then.

RaceName: Moloney's Bar And Music Venue Maiden
Spotlight: Big prices, but has shown plenty so far; just ahead of 79-rated foe when second over 9.5f at Gowran, so he'll need a bit more; yard won Leopardstown maiden on Thursday.

RaceName: Moloney's Bar And Music Venue Maiden
Spotlight: Bolger-bred went from 800,000gns as a yearling to 20,000gns 3yo last month; better of two March AW runs for Charlie Appleby when second over this trip at Chelmsford.

RaceName: Moloney's Bar And Music Venue Maiden
Spotlight: Elzaam colt; dam unraced half-sister to Scandinavian 1m-8.6f winner, out of 1m2f winning half-sister to Listed winners Coupe De Ville (1m 2yo) and Fantastico Robert (US 1m1f); young trainer having a good season, but this one is best watched unless backed.

RaceName: Moloney's Bar And Music Venue Maiden
Spotlight: Half-brother to winners Snowcapped (Listed-placed 7f/mile) and It's Snowing (6f AW 2yo), 16s, yard second string, ran respectably following a slow start when beaten around 9l at Gowran in early June (yard won it with favourite).

RaceName: Moloney's Bar And Music Venue Maiden
Spotlight: Didn't seem to stay 1m4f latest but earlier runs, including 3l fourth over C&D, make him worthy of his mark.

RaceName: Moloney's Bar And Music Venue Maiden
Spotlight: Sea The Stars half-sister to yard's Group 3 winner Starford; lovely debut over a mile at Naas, missed the break and was green, finished well under a hand ride when fourth to a better-fancied stablemate.

RaceName: Moloney's Bar And Music Venue Maiden
OwnerName: Team Valor International LLC & A Oliver
Spotlight: Both runs over C&D; beaten a length on debut but 3l fifth last time was of equal merit; closely matched with Will You Stop on that form; headgear.

RaceName: Sky Bet Strensall Stakes (Group 3)
Spotlight: Won the Group 3 Earl Of Sefton at Newmarket (1m1f, good) on reappearance and mid-division in Group 1s on next two runs; third of five to subsequent International winner Item here (10.2f, good to firm) last time and has leading claims back down in trip/grade; cheekpieces go on; has won on good to soft.

RaceName: Sky Bet Strensall Stakes (Group 3)
Spotlight: Unplaced favourite in the Royal Hunt Cup at Royal Ascot (1m, good to firm) but bounced back to win the competitive Golden Mile at Glorious Goodwood (1m, good to firm) three weeks ago; defied joint-top weight last time and he could give a good account now up in grade; has shown promise on soft.

RaceName: Sky Bet Strensall Stakes (Group 3)
Spotlight: Unraced on slow ground; won two handicaps in a row at Meydan (1m1f/9.5f, good) in February before Group 2 second there (1m1f, good) and he returned from a break with good third in the Listed Wolferton Stakes at Royal Ascot (1m2f, good to firm); things haven't gone to plan on his two starts since but a line can be put through Goodwood as he got no run; interesting contender.

RaceName: Sky Bet Strensall Stakes (Group 3)
Spotlight: 0-6 in Group/Listed races since debut win in 2024 and others have stronger recent form; however, he's been a close second in Listed races on both starts this year, weaving around runners before keeping on strongly at Leopardstown (1m, yielding to soft) on the first occasion then perhaps finding the drop back to 7f against him at the Curragh (good); he's Aidan O'Brien's sole runner and this new trip could be right up his street; cheekpieces go on.

RaceName: Sky Bet Strensall Stakes (Group 3)
Spotlight: All starts on good/faster; won the Group 2 Celebration Mile at Goodwood last August and bagged 1m Listed win at Ascot this May; close third in hot 1m1f conditions race at Goodwood three weeks ago and could be involved.

RaceName: Sky Bet Strensall Stakes (Group 3)
Spotlight: Went very close in Group 3 Diomed Stakes at Epsom in June (8.5f, good to soft; won same race 12 months earlier) and has continued in good form, justifying even-money favouritism in Listed race at Newbury (1m2f, good to firm) last time; he's firmly in calculations.

RaceName: Sky Bet Strensall Stakes (Group 3)
OwnerName: Julie And David R Martin And Dan Hall
Spotlight: Slow ground would be a worry (non-runner due to unsuitable good to soft here on Thursday) and he's unraced over this far; however, this front-runner has an extremely solid record in 1m handicaps here and was a Group 2 runner-up at Ascot (1m) last July; capable of bold bid if conditions suit.

RaceName: Sky Bet Strensall Stakes (Group 3)
Spotlight: Group 2 winner at Longchamp (1m, very soft) last October; not at the same level in the USA this year on his three starts for Miguel Clement but those were on firm ground and he could be a different proposition now back on a slower surface on his first start for George Scott; he's one to consider.

RaceName: Sky Bet Strensall Stakes (Group 3)
Spotlight: 3yo who has got better with each run this season and impressed in the Group 3 Meld at Leopardstown (1m1f, good) last month before finishing second in the Group 3 Gordon at Glorious Goodwood (1m4f, good to firm) under a 3lb penalty (same today); runner-up in a Group 2 on yielding to soft last September; this versatile sort could be in the mix back down in trip.

RaceName: Sky Bet Strensall Stakes (Group 3)
OwnerName: Exors Of The Late Sheikh Mohammed Obaid
Spotlight: Won on debut here (7f, good) last June and made it 2-3 as 2yo when making all in the Group 3 Autumn Stakes at Newmarket (1m, good to firm) last October; reappeared with fine front-running third in the Group 1 Poule d'Essai Des Poulains at Longchamp (1m, very soft) in May; down the field in the Group 1 Prix du Jockey Club at Chantilly (10.5f, good) three weeks later but has had a break since and is very much of interest judged on his previous form.

RaceName: Sky Bet Strensall Stakes (Group 3)
Spotlight: Promise on first three starts (including on soft/good to soft) before winning Wolverhampton maiden (8.6f, AW) in June; followed up in big-field handicap at the Curragh (1m1f, good) in first-time cheekpieces (retained); this is a much tougher test of his credentials and Tom Marquand rides stablemate Saber Strike, but he's very well bred and in top hands; not ruled out.

RaceName: Sky Bet Strensall Stakes (Group 3)
Spotlight: All five starts on good/good to firm; made it 2-2 with 7f Listed win at Newmarket in May and has shaped in 7f/1m Group 3 races on his last two starts (including here) as though this new trip could be a good fit; not discounted in first-time tongue-tie; the blinkers adopted last time are left off.

RaceName: Celebrating National Racehorse Week Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Opened his account over hurdles in a Stratford handicap (2m, good to firm) in June off a mark of 99 and ran a solid race when runner-up off 3lb higher at Worcester last month; more is required under a penalty back in novice company against a couple of these but he shouldn't be far away.

RaceName: Celebrating National Racehorse Week Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
OwnerName: D Summersby J May W Dodd
Spotlight: Beaten a long way in a bumper, two points and a maiden and a novice hurdle (80-1 and 200-1).

RaceName: Celebrating National Racehorse Week Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Showed little in point bumpers and two point starts (2m4f-3m) but offered more when a well-held fourth at Worcester (2m, good) in a first-time hood on hurdle debut; hood removed here and he looks one for the longer term.

RaceName: Celebrating National Racehorse Week Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Confirmed the promise of her Irish point form when making a winning start to her hurdle career on stable debut at Uttoxeter (2m, good), staying on best under Harry Cobden; may want further in time and this track may be on the sharp side, but she remains a leading player under her penalty.

RaceName: Celebrating National Racehorse Week Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Hinted at ability on bumper debut but has not progressed from that and finished tailed off on both starts over hurdles in July; easy to look elsewhere.

RaceName: ML Lynch Civil Engineering Ltd. Maiden Hurdle (Div II)
Spotlight: Dual Flat winner in Britain on good-to-firm; improved on moderate hurdles debut when beaten 17l at Listowel on good 84 days ago having raced plenty keen; each-way claims if building on that.

RaceName: ML Lynch Civil Engineering Ltd. Maiden Hurdle (Div II)
Spotlight: Mid-division on debut in Punchestown bumper, but improved plenty at Ballinrobe when running out a ready 4.75l winner; form hasn't worked out yet, but he was impressive and is an interesting hurdling debutant.

RaceName: ML Lynch Civil Engineering Ltd. Maiden Hurdle (Div II)
Spotlight: Sole win in 14 starts on Flat came here over 1m on good last month off 75; set to finish a decent third on hurdles debut at Tipperary in October; that form entitles him to be considered.

RaceName: ML Lynch Civil Engineering Ltd. Maiden Hurdle (Div II)
Spotlight: Dual Flat winner on good-to-firm in Britain; likely to have finished second but for unseating at the last at Galway on hurdles debut 21 days ago; that rates strong form so a similar effort could be good enough.

RaceName: ML Lynch Civil Engineering Ltd. Maiden Hurdle (Div II)
Spotlight: Little to suggest he can win this based on two hurdle runs; well behind Sea Eagle last time; tongue-tie tried.

RaceName: ML Lynch Civil Engineering Ltd. Maiden Hurdle (Div II)
Spotlight: Pulled up on debut in bumper 163 days ago; others preferred.

RaceName: ML Lynch Civil Engineering Ltd. Maiden Hurdle (Div II)
Spotlight: Rated 95 after four hurdle runs; unlikely to be good enough to feature here.

RaceName: ML Lynch Civil Engineering Ltd. Maiden Hurdle (Div II)
Spotlight: Nothing in first to runs to suggest that he can win a maiden hurdle.

RaceName: ML Lynch Civil Engineering Ltd. Maiden Hurdle (Div II)
Spotlight: Moderate hurdles debut, set to finish way behind Golden Handshake; unlikely contender.

RaceName: ML Lynch Civil Engineering Ltd. Maiden Hurdle (Div II)
Spotlight: Ocovango gelding; dam 2m6f chase/3m hurdle winner; makes belated debut and best watched.

RaceName: ML Lynch Civil Engineering Ltd. Maiden Hurdle (Div II)
Spotlight: Set to run a big race on point-to-point debut in 2024 before falling; returned after long absence when neck second to Like An Ocean at Roscommon last month; disappointed up in trip on softer ground 18 days ago; bit to find with principals.

RaceName: ML Lynch Civil Engineering Ltd. Maiden Hurdle (Div II)
Spotlight: Massaat gelding; 8,000gns yearling; half-brother to winners Cape Coast (1m4f/1m6f; RPR 98), Conundrum (1m/1m2f Flat, 81; 2m hurdle) and Annie Agnew (2m1f hurdle); dam Italian Listed-placed 7.5f-1m3f winner (inc 2yo; 101), half-sister to 1m Group 2 winner Fanunalter; one of two for stable and first string; market can guide.

RaceName: ML Lynch Civil Engineering Ltd. Maiden Hurdle (Div II)
Spotlight: Reasonable runs at Limerick over hurdles and in a Thurles bumper but overall form suggests she's not up to winning this.

RaceName: ML Lynch Civil Engineering Ltd. Maiden Hurdle (Div II)
Spotlight: Beaten a long way both hurdle starts; one for handicaps

RaceName: ML Lynch Civil Engineering Ltd. Maiden Hurdle (Div II)
Spotlight: Tailed off on debut 14 days ago; no reason to fancy.

RaceName: Virgin Bet Supports Safe Gambling Handicap
Spotlight: First of two wins over C&D came in this contest in 2024 off 4lb lower; had a fruitful AW winter campaign; reported to have met with a setback when being readied for Chester's May meeting and returned only when beating just one home in the Golden Mile at Goodwood (1m, good to firm) recently; has a high draw to contend with here and is 3lb higher than his last winning mark.

RaceName: Virgin Bet Supports Safe Gambling Handicap
Spotlight: Landed a Group 3 at Kempton last September as a juvenile before finishing fourth in the Middle Park Stakes at Newmarket, both over 6f; highly tried without success this term and although his yard is going great guns, his mark looks high at present.

RaceName: Virgin Bet Supports Safe Gambling Handicap
OwnerName: Exors Of The Late Sheikh Mohammed Obaid
Spotlight: Previously trained in Australia, he still looks to be finding his level in Britain after three unplaced efforts; dons first-time cheekpieces but best watched until he tells us more.

RaceName: Virgin Bet Supports Safe Gambling Handicap
Spotlight: 0-16 on turf but usually runs his race; runner-up at this track (10.5f, good) when last seen in May; may find this on the sharp side having not been seen in races less than 1m since his juvenile days.

RaceName: Virgin Bet Supports Safe Gambling Handicap
OwnerName: Exors Of The Late Sheikh Mohammed Obaid
Spotlight: Absent nearly two years after making a winning debut at Newmarket in 2024, he has made up for lost time recently and bagged his third win on handicap debut at Thirsk (7f, good; 15-8) three weeks ago; there should be plenty more to come from him and he needs to be taken seriously here off 3lb higher.

RaceName: Virgin Bet Supports Safe Gambling Handicap
Spotlight: Made a winning return in a Southwell maiden (7f, AW) in March but found out in three Group/Listed races subsequently; gelded before his ninth of 13 at Goodwood (7f, good to firm) three weeks ago on handicap debut; looks a shade high in the weights.

RaceName: Virgin Bet Supports Safe Gambling Handicap
Spotlight: Hasn't won on turf for over two years but landed a four-timer on the AW in the spring; has been running consistently on turf since, admittedly starting to look exposed but he should run his race.

RaceName: Virgin Bet Supports Safe Gambling Handicap
Spotlight: Yet to fire this season but landed his third win here when successful in this race last year (good to firm) off 4lb higher; he has also been placed twice at this track and can never be written off around here.

RaceName: Virgin Bet Supports Safe Gambling Handicap
Spotlight: Hasn't fired yet this term but needs conditions softer than good to show his best form; has dropped down to a tempting mark but is 0-3 around here and is at his best at Goodwood and Epsom.

RaceName: Virgin Bet Supports Safe Gambling Handicap
Spotlight: Formerly trained by Jessica Harrington in Ireland where he won a Galway maiden; sold to join current yard for 33,000gns last month and made an immediate impact by winning over C&D (good); has been raised 7lb and has an outside draw but may still have more to offer.

RaceName: Virgin Bet Supports Safe Gambling Handicap
Spotlight: Normally ridden to be produced late, as when successful at Salisbury (7f, good) in June, but was given a straightforward ride to land a claimer over C&D (good) 20 days ago; this looks tougher however and more is required.

RaceName: Virgin Bet Supports Safe Gambling Handicap
Spotlight: Landed his third race when successful from a flag start at Ripon (6f, good) in May; may have needed the run when sixth of 12 at Hamilton (6f, good) on his first run since 11 days ago; races beyond 7f for the first time.

RaceName: Virgin Bet Supports Safe Gambling Handicap
Spotlight: 7lb higher than her last winning mark but has a course record of 1212; cannot be written off.

RaceName: Twyford Down Cutting Handicap
Spotlight: All four wins at 6f and not on an impossible mark even with top weight; however, he's not easily trusted after his last two efforts.

RaceName: Twyford Down Cutting Handicap
Spotlight: Signed off last season with a head success off this mark on the Rowley Mile (6f, good); he appeared to be running into form before the new cheekpieces backfired at Doncaster; makes the shortlist.

RaceName: Twyford Down Cutting Handicap
Spotlight: Can leads; dual winner at two; below best over 5f at Goodwood last time but had been running well in 6f handicaps and those were stronger races; stall 1 might not be ideal but enters the reckoning.

RaceName: Twyford Down Cutting Handicap
Spotlight: Dual winner; 0-5 for Stuart Williams but had been holding his own in 7f handicaps until a lesser show last time; whether he's quick enough for 6f is the glaring concern (all 23 runs from 7f to 1m2f).

RaceName: Twyford Down Cutting Handicap
Spotlight: Went close over C&D last week in a race he won two years earlier; now 3lb higher and they claimed 5lb last time, so may need more.

RaceName: Twyford Down Cutting Handicap
Spotlight: 6f AW maiden winner in Ireland and won a 7f AW novice for Ben Haslam in April; went close in one of his three subsequent handicaps and that was over 6f; sold in July for 47,000gns; not dismissed.

RaceName: Twyford Down Cutting Handicap
Spotlight: Doing well for his new yard and nicely on top at the finish in a big field at York a month ago (6f, good to firm); up 5lb but looks a big player.

RaceName: Twyford Down Cutting Handicap
Spotlight: Won a Newbury maiden and followed up in a C&D handicap in June off 4lb lower; down the field at the July meeting and raced freely when no match for the winner in a small field at Leicester; remains open to improvement and a tongue-tie is added.

RaceName: Twyford Down Cutting Handicap
OwnerName: J P Morris, Mrs V A Tunnicliffe Et Al
Spotlight: Won on the Rowley Mile in May (6f, good; 4lb lower) and last time finished sixth of 26 at Glorious Goodwood, which wasn't a bad run; usually ridden from behind so needs a strong pace which he might get.

RaceName: Twyford Down Cutting Handicap
Spotlight: Had been running well but has performed miserably in his last two races when awkward at the start both times.

RaceName: Twyford Down Cutting Handicap
Spotlight: Has won over 1m but recent efforts at 6f and after his C&D win he fared best of those held up when third last week; this could pan out more favourably for him.

RaceName: Twyford Down Cutting Handicap
Spotlight: In-form 9yo whose last four runs have been over C&D; failed narrowly under a penalty two weeks ago (behind Fifty Nifty) but 1lb lower here and should be involved.

RaceName: Twyford Down Cutting Handicap
Spotlight: C&D winner last August off this mark when with Stuart Williams; however, pretty much tailed off in this season's races.

RaceName: Mitsubishi Electric Handicap
Spotlight: 7f and Cork not really his bag, so not a bad effort at all when beaten less than 2l in Listed company last time; previous fourth of 20 in British-dominated Scurry handicap was creditable too, and will have every chance if he gets the right set-up.

RaceName: Mitsubishi Electric Handicap
Spotlight: Won off 91 at Navan (5f) in May, but it's been a struggle since and hard to fancy at present.

RaceName: Mitsubishi Electric Handicap
OwnerName: Anthony Paul Smurfit & Samuel M Mencoff
Spotlight: Prominent racer followed up Naas win with 3l fourth of 22 at York in June; that valuable race has worked out pretty well, as it usually does, and it was a good effort for an Irish sprinter in such a competitive British sprint.

RaceName: Mitsubishi Electric Handicap
OwnerName: Kildare Racing Syndicate & Kilmichael Racing Syndicate
Spotlight: Promising debut over C&D in May 2025 before easily scoring at Dundalk by 3.25l; ordinary form, but looked potentially useful that day; off over a year and would be a smart effort to beat these on handicap debut.

RaceName: Mitsubishi Electric Handicap
Spotlight: Succession of good runs over various sprint trips here this year; won the Rockingham in June and good second over that 5f distance last time; previously, had four of these behind when third in the Scurry over an extended 6f, which was a bit too far.

RaceName: Mitsubishi Electric Handicap
Spotlight: Last win came in last year's Scurry here over slightly farther; some good runs this season, but basically he's in the handicapper's grip; went back up 4lb for Galway second over 7f, not as effective over 5f when favourite here last time.

RaceName: Mitsubishi Electric Handicap
Spotlight: A little bit hard to figure him out but, to be charitable, probably still learning his trade; unlucky fourth to Chicago Pope early in the season; staying-on fifth of 20 in the Scurry here was a good effort; ridden 2f out and just stuck on one-paced when third at Naas latest; visored last twice, now goes unaided.

RaceName: Mitsubishi Electric Handicap
Spotlight: Sole win in 25 starts came when he beat Keke over C&D last year; couple of excuses this term (raced on wrong side at Naas last time) and has inched back down to winning mark; blinkers replace visor.

RaceName: Mitsubishi Electric Handicap
Spotlight: Reasonable AW form in Britain before being picked up for 15,000gns in July; mid-field in 7f claimer on stable debut; will do well to get competitive in this, unless new headgear works.

RaceName: Mitsubishi Electric Handicap
Spotlight: Won Cork maiden over this trip on third start; last of 12 over 5f here on handicap debut; doubtless she's better than that, but hard to face into all the same.

RaceName: Mitsubishi Electric Handicap
OwnerName: Mrs S Bury & Ralph Kelly & Odhran O'Neill & Thomas Cox
Spotlight: Has been a revelation since dropping back to this trip with the addition of blinkers, and being ridden forward; just worn down late at Naas (Gavoo third) last time; wrong at the weights, so 5lb higher now.

RaceName: Mitsubishi Electric Handicap
Spotlight: Three wins here; struck for the first time since 2024 when winning at Navan in June; may have benefitted from track position (only runner-up and himself raced far side), but in fairness, second won lately; missed an engagement here earlier this month and profile suggests layoff not ideal; 3lb wrong, but top 'bug' rides.

RaceName: Sky Bet Melrose Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Made it four wins on the spin when landing the Group 2 Queen's Vase at Royal Ascot (1m6f, good to firm; versatile ground-wise); down the field in the Group 1 Grand Prix de Paris at Longchamp since but judged on his previous form he could be on an advantageous mark for today's handicap debut.

RaceName: Sky Bet Melrose Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Suited by the step up to 1m4f when getting the better of a terrific battle to win at Glorious Goodwood on second handicap start (good to firm; front two clear); 1m6f could prompt further improvement and his trainer has won two of the last seven runnings; showed promise on soft on debut; key player.

RaceName: Sky Bet Melrose Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Bumped into the highly progressive Lost Boys when short-headed on handicap debut at Sandown (1m2f, good; unraced on slower) in April and bounced back from an underwhelming Royal Ascot run to win at Glorious Goodwood (1m3f, good to firm) in first-time cheekpieces (retained); dam was a 15.5f Listed winner (heavy) and he could take another step forward now tackling 1m6f.

RaceName: Sky Bet Melrose Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Looked one to follow when keeping on for third on handicap debut in the London Gold Cup at Newbury (1m2f, good); however, he's failed to settle and finished soundly beaten over 1m4f on his last two starts and, while Goodwood may not have suited last time, he arrives with something to prove.

RaceName: Sky Bet Melrose Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Prominent racer who showed improvement to win by 4l at Newbury (1m4f, good to soft) in June and followed up at Newmarket (1m6f, good to firm) last month; had just a nose to spare last time and is 5lb higher today but he's clearly progressive and his trainer has won three of the last six runnings.

RaceName: Sky Bet Melrose Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Has won on various ground; strong finish for 4l sixth of 19 in the King George V Stakes at Royal Ascot (1m4f) and that handicap form has worked out exceptionally well; as expected he was suited by the step up to 1m6f when winning at Ascot last month and could have more to offer at this trip.

RaceName: Sky Bet Melrose Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: All starts on good/good to firm; made it 2-3 in handicaps when upped in trip to beat Who's Lope over C&D in June; a line can be put through his subsequent second of three at Sandown as they went no gallop; up in grade today but unexposed at the trip and he's not ruled out.

RaceName: Sky Bet Melrose Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Placed on first three starts (8.3f-1m2f, including on good to soft) before justifying favouritism on handicap/AW debut at Newcastle four weeks ago (12.4f; Eniac third); that latest form has been franked by the runner-up and there's every chance that this one will be suited by 1m6f; one to consider.

RaceName: Sky Bet Melrose Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Improved upon his three maiden runs (1m-9.5f) when upped to 12.3f on handicap debut at the Galway festival (yielding), beaten just a neck in that big field; he's trained by Willie Mullins and wears first-time cheekpieces today, and there can be optimism that he will continue to progress; respected.

RaceName: Sky Bet Melrose Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Won at Beverley (1m4f, good to firm) in May on third run and close second to My Ballyquinn on handicap debut over C&D in June (good; led); further improvement is necessary but he's just the type his trainer, who has won three of the last six runnings, does very well with; unraced on slow ground.

RaceName: Sky Bet Melrose Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: 2yo maiden winner (good to soft) who has run some good races in defeat in 1m4f handicaps this year, including here (good) in May and when third at Ascot (good to firm) recently in a first-time visor (retained); it's possible 1m6f will suit but others in this line-up appear to be more progressive.

RaceName: Sky Bet Melrose Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: He's raced ten times but has shown improved form of late, winning narrowly in a small field at Newbury (1m3f, good to firm) then second to Into The Light at Glorious Goodwood (1m3f, good to firm); stayed on well last time and could better that performance now at 1m6f; unproven on slow ground.

RaceName: Sky Bet Melrose Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Won at Dundalk (1m4f, AW) in April on second start and kept on for close second on handicap debut at Leopardstown (1m4f, good) in May behind one on the middle leg of a hat-trick; failed to settle and had to wait for a clear run when third in first-time cheekpieces (retained) at Down Royal (1m5f, soft) two months ago and that form has also been franked by the winner; a strong gallop today would help and he could be capable of considerably better.

RaceName: Sky Bet Melrose Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Won a maiden at Pontefract (1m2f, good) last month on his third start; it's still very early days but he finished held in sixth behind a couple of these at Glorious Goodwood (1m3f, good to firm) and others are preferred.

RaceName: Sky Bet Melrose Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Third of 15 on the Monday of the Galway festival last month (12.3f, yielding) and found a surge of improvement in a first-time hood to demolish a big field there (1m6f, yielding to soft) four days later; hit with a whopping 15lb rise but that may not stop him given his dominance last time.

RaceName: Sky Bet Melrose Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Seven-race maiden who is 2lb out of the handicap but he showed promise for Donnacha O'Brien and ran a big race on stable debut at Newcastle (12.4f, AW) four weeks ago, travelling well and keeping on nicely for 1l third behind Glory Road; this longer trip could suit and he's an interesting contender.

RaceName: Sky Bet Melrose Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: 2-2 in handicaps, both three-runner races, the first by 12l at Lingfield (11.6f, good to firm) and the latest at Sandown (1m6f, good to firm); they went no gallop last time and, from out of the handicap, he's 8lb higher in this much hotter race, but it remains to be seen where his ceiling lies.

RaceName: Happy 80th Birthday John Lane Conditional Jockeys' Handicap Chase
Spotlight: In fine form after blinkers were added in early summer, winning at Perth (2m4f, good to soft) and Hexham (3m, good), before disappointing at Market Rasen last month when reportedly unsuited by the track; retains chase potential and could prove up to this mark if bouncing back.

RaceName: Happy 80th Birthday John Lane Conditional Jockeys' Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Four-time chase winner who has returned to form on his last two starts, both over C&D, latest when just under 2l behind My Girl Katie; 2lb better off with that rival despite a 3lb rise and should be thereabouts again.

RaceName: Happy 80th Birthday John Lane Conditional Jockeys' Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Just 1-18 over fences but generally consistent and has plenty of placed efforts to his name; below par on his last two starts (2m5f here) and now tackles his longest trip to date, though he stays 3m; remains on a tough-looking mark and others appeal more for the win.

RaceName: Happy 80th Birthday John Lane Conditional Jockeys' Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Largely consistent mare who justified support back from an absence when landing a third chase win last month, her second over C&D; up 5lb but Alix Balfe claims 7lb and she'll likely give her running and be thereabouts.

RaceName: Happy 80th Birthday John Lane Conditional Jockeys' Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Four-time chase winner who went close over C&D in June on third run back from a long absence, before tailing off behind My Girl Katie here last month; a player if that is forgiven, with promising Rian Corcoran booked.

RaceName: Happy 80th Birthday John Lane Conditional Jockeys' Handicap Chase
Spotlight: Won an Exeter hurdle race off a mark of 74 on stable debut in December but has failed to match that level since, including in two starts over fences; last month's reappearance may have been needed when a well-held last of six over hurdles but he has a bit to prove back over fences, despite his lower chase mark.

RaceName: Adare Manor Opportunity Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Struggled on handicap debut at Cork but bounced back since with two placed efforts at Wexford (2m1f, good); didn't find much for pressure when fifth at Wexford over this trip 15 days ago; on a nice mark but questionable whether he relishes this trip.

RaceName: Adare Manor Opportunity Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Maiden showed promise in bumpers in 2024 but has disappointed a bit in handicap company; good third at Limerick (2m4f, good) in July; matched that with 5l third at Tramore nine days ago; needs more but definitely capable; tongue-tie added with existing cheekpieces.

RaceName: Adare Manor Opportunity Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: 0-15 over hurdles; won point-to-point in February; no impact in hunter chases in the spring; well beaten in handicap hurdle at Cork 19 days ago; step up in trip will suit but needs more.

RaceName: Adare Manor Opportunity Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Maiden who looked ready to strike when third at Cork (2m1f, good) last month but disappointed as well-backed favourite over same C&D next time; bounced back to some extent when beaten 6.5l at Tramore nine days ago over similar trip (Pure Logic 1.25l ahead); should remain competitive.

RaceName: Adare Manor Opportunity Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Didn't run badly when eighth at Limerick in April (2m, soft); little to shout about otherwise and pulled up behind Andyourbirdcansing 41 days ago; plenty to find.

RaceName: Adare Manor Opportunity Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Beaten 20l plus in four maiden hurdles and a handicap; off 672 days and has switched to Gavin Cromwell; stable do well with recruits and it's interesting she's been persevered with; market confidence would have to be taken very seriously.

RaceName: Adare Manor Opportunity Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Sole win came at Tramore (20.5f, yielding) in April off 5lb lower, pulling well clear with second; ran fine at Clonmel off revised mark; unseated back at Tramore when under pressure and beaten 19l, but didn't enjoy a clean run; contender.

RaceName: Adare Manor Opportunity Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Off the track two years and progressed from Listowel reappearance to make late headway into fourth at Ballinrobe (2m1f, good) last month; unseated at first 15 days ago; chance if building on that Ballinrobe effort.

RaceName: Adare Manor Opportunity Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Maiden who has some decent placed form, most notably at Limerick (2m, soft) in April when beaten 1.75l into third; well-held third last twice, including over C&D; step back up in distance should suit; usually ridden off the pace.

RaceName: Adare Manor Opportunity Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Well beat in maiden hurdles and fared no better on handicap debut 29 days ago; hard to fancy.

RaceName: Adare Manor Opportunity Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Has struggled in three maidens and two handicap runs; others far more convincing.

RaceName: Adare Manor Opportunity Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Dual handicap hurdle winner, latest at Kilbeggan (3m1f, good) in September off 1lb lower, beating very well-treated Rising Dust; not gone on from that but more positive run at Kilbeggan last month; tame effort over shorter last time and is at his best over further.

RaceName: Adare Manor Opportunity Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Point-to-point form this year nothing to shout about and beaten a fair way in maiden hurdle 36 days ago; others preferred.

RaceName: Adare Manor Opportunity Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Step in right direction when a keeping-on fourth at Limerick (2m4f, soft) in May but no impression at Sligo latest behind same rival; needs to bounce back.

RaceName: Adare Manor Opportunity Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Sole win in 25 starts came at Cork (2m1f, good) a year ago; back on that mark but poor on last hurdles run at Punchestown and pulled up over fences here last month; capable but needs to shrug off latest effort.

RaceName: Virgin Bet Chester Stakes (Listed Race)
Spotlight: Chased home Lambourn in last year's Chester Vase and Derby (also third to him in the Irish Derby); missed the second half of last season but showed he's still as good as ever when defeating the reopposing Lady Vivian in 2m Sandown Listed race (good) last month; raced freely and weakened quickly in the Goodwood Cup with cheekpieces added (quickly discarded) but he can bounce back with his sights lowered today.

RaceName: Virgin Bet Chester Stakes (Listed Race)
Spotlight: Low-mileage 5yo who progressed into a really smart performer at up to 1m6f at Meydan over the winter and made a sound return to Britain when chasing home Al Aasy in a Beverley Listed race (1m4f, good to firm) seven weeks ago; going on the soft side of good would be an unknown but he holds good form claims.

RaceName: Virgin Bet Chester Stakes (Listed Race)
Spotlight: Fine third from the front in the Chester Cup (2m2f, good) on his first start for Richard Hughes; proved way too headstrong to give himself a chance of lasting home in the Copper Horse at Royal Ascot next time but ridden with restraint and saw things out a lot better when fourth of seven in 2m Newbury handicap (good to firm) since; has a bit to find on the figures back at Listed level.

RaceName: Virgin Bet Chester Stakes (Listed Race)
Spotlight: Sold for 600,000gns after winning a 1m6f Ascot Listed race (good to soft) for Andrew Balding last autumn; didn't make the expected impact over hurdles for Nicky Henderson earlier this year (pulled up in Triumph at Cheltenham when last seen) but resumes his Flat career back with a yard which is in tremendous form.

RaceName: Virgin Bet Chester Stakes (Listed Race)
Spotlight: Won Group 3 at Saint-Cloud (10.5f, good) last May; respectable efforts at Listed/Group 3 level for current yard this summer but will need to pull out more for the longer trip if he's to resume winning ways.

RaceName: Virgin Bet Chester Stakes (Listed Race)
Spotlight: Progressed into a useful staying handicapper in the second half of 2024; gelded ahead of this belated return; has plenty to find on form and might be using this as a prep ahead of a return to handicap company (entered in Cesarewitch).

RaceName: Virgin Bet Chester Stakes (Listed Race)
Spotlight: Her previous course visit resulted in a handicap win over the extended 1m4f on good ground (acts on good to soft) at the 2025 May meeting; campaigned at Group/Listed level since, running her best race when 2.75l second of four to Lazy Griff at Sandown (2m, good) last month; 3lb better off with Charlie Johnston's charge this time; Ralph Beckett has won this three times since 2021.

RaceName: Virgin Bet Chester Stakes (Listed Race)
Spotlight: Reliable type whose wins have come in 1m2f and 1m6f handicaps; good fourth in this race 12 months ago and showed she retains her ability when fifth in another Listed event at Newmarket (1m4f, good to firm) on her reappearance three weeks ago.

RaceName: Hargreaves Services PLC Handicap
Spotlight: Has mixed record this season but won a match race in June and was seemingly aided by a first-time hood when very close second at Doncaster (1m, good to firm) a week ago; on the premises if in the right mood again.

RaceName: Hargreaves Services PLC Handicap
Spotlight: Showed only minor promise in his three qualifying races (7f-8.3f) and is not obviously well treated for this handicap debut but remains unexposed; worth a glance in the betting.

RaceName: Hargreaves Services PLC Handicap
Spotlight: Sometimes races a bit too freely but ran well before fading into fourth over C&D (good) in June and returns here after keeping on well for second in tactical race at Ffos Las (1m, good) ten days ago; still on a workable mark; might be the answer.

RaceName: Hargreaves Services PLC Handicap
Spotlight: Kept on well for clearcut success in six-runner race at Yarmouth (1m, good to firm) three weeks ago, his second win over that C&D this season; moves back up from Class 6 after a 6lb rise but is evidently in good nick.

RaceName: Hargreaves Services PLC Handicap
Spotlight: Returned to form with C&D (good to firm) win for James Ferguson in June and was respectable fourth at Windsor (1m, good to firm) on last month's first run for Tom Clover; tends to face a bit too freely so it will be interesting to see whether switch from blinkers to a first-time hood pay dividends.

RaceName: Hargreaves Services PLC Handicap
OwnerName: L J Vaessen And Stephen Barber
Spotlight: Outran 33-1 odds when second of six in slowly run C&D (good to firm) novice last month, her third start, but the value of that form is open to question and she was remote when last of four over 1m2f here three weeks ago.

RaceName: Hargreaves Services PLC Handicap
Spotlight: Three-time AW winner for James Ferguson in early part of this year and placed on both subsequent turf starts (1m, good to firm/good); didn't fire on Tapeta last month but makes stable debut from a workable mark.

RaceName: Alpha Centauri Debutante Stakes (Group 2) (Fillies)
OwnerName: Flaxman Stables, Mrs Magnier, M Tabor, D Smith
Spotlight: Regally bred Sea The Stars filly; narrowly denied on debut on soft ground at Leopardstown (7f) by Blonde Over Blue; gained compensation on next start in decisive fashion in a C&D maiden (good); saw off the fast-finishing Dancing Destiny by a head upped to Group 3 company back at Leopardstown a month ago (Blonde Over Blue fourth); likely more to come and preferred by Lordan.

RaceName: Alpha Centauri Debutante Stakes (Group 2) (Fillies)
Spotlight: Lope De Vega filly took the scalp of Alpha on debut at Leopardstown (7f, soft); however, proved no match for that rival (or Dancing Destiny) when upped to Group 3 company back there on latest; Browne McMonagle jumps ship and tongue tie goes on now.

RaceName: Alpha Centauri Debutante Stakes (Group 2) (Fillies)
Spotlight: Magna Grecia filly has run five times; won her maiden on debut at Roscommon (7.5f, good); added a Listed heat at Naas (1m, good) on penultimate; flew home for a head second behind Alpha in Leopardstown Group 3 latest (7f, good); should be thereabouts again.

RaceName: Alpha Centauri Debutante Stakes (Group 2) (Fillies)
Spotlight: Saxon Warrior filly is 0-2 but those two defeats were behind the top class Sun Goddess; finished 5l behind her when runner up on debut here (6f, good); closed the gap to 0.75l in the Airlie Stud Stakes back here on her second start (6f, gd-fm); the way she finished that day suggested this longer trip will suit; preferred by Browne McMonagle and an intriguing runner.

RaceName: Alpha Centauri Debutante Stakes (Group 2) (Fillies)
OwnerName: Michael Tabor & Derrick Smith & Mrs John Magnier & Flaxman S
Spotlight: Off the mark at the fourth attempt in maidens, bolting up over C&D (gd-fm) in a first time hood which is retained; finished 6l behind Alpha when runner up in a C&D maiden in June (when Wayne Lordan rode); can't be discounted upped in class but this time Lordan prefers Alpha.

RaceName: Sky Bet City Of York Stakes (Group 1)
Spotlight: From three visits to York he's won a Gimcrack and finished an unlucky-in-running second in this 12 months ago; gelding operation has triggered a further upturn in his fortunes, winning Listed/Group 2 races over this trip (good ground) on either side of a close fifth in the 6f Group 1 sprint at Royal Ascot (running on); it was his second run in as many days at Glorious Goodwood (after winning the Lennox) when traffic issues scuppered all hope in the Sussex Stakes; the worry is this week's rain as he's had precious little racing on ground softer than good and hasn't shone when he has.

RaceName: Sky Bet City Of York Stakes (Group 1)
Spotlight: Unraced at York but he does go on any ground, and his career-best form came on soft when impressing in a 7f Group 2 at Doncaster last September; creditable effort conceding weight all round when runner-up to Paborus in a Group 3 over 6f (AW) on his return to Britain in June and it's best to put a line through his run behind Lake Forest at Glorious Goodwood (7f) as he raced far too freely off a slacking pace; with a truer gallop on the cards and no ground issues, he could be a lively one.

RaceName: Sky Bet City Of York Stakes (Group 1)
Spotlight: Form figures of 1311571 in a visor; a graduate from the handicap ranks and he didn't have all that much in hand when the 6-4 winner of a Group 3 in Ireland in June on latest start (7f, soft); looks up against it now he's dining at the top table, unless transformed by a wind operation.

RaceName: Sky Bet City Of York Stakes (Group 1)
Spotlight: Not the first time he's failed to fire at Ascot when a disappointing favourite in the Queen Anne, having previously looked better than ever in showing his trademark turn of foot to win the Lockinge at Newbury (good); renowned as a top-class domestic/international miler but he didn't run badly in last year's July Cup and should be fully effective at 7f; while fast ground shows him at his brilliant best, he nearly won a French Group 1 last season on good to soft; commands the utmost respect.

RaceName: Sky Bet City Of York Stakes (Group 1)
Spotlight: Strike-rate of 5-8 and long absences are a feature in his profile; back from another to produce career-best form in beating Marvelman at Newcastle in June (6f AW) but he'd be no certainty to confirm those placings on 5lb worse terms, while there are plenty of others to worry about; on the plus side, he remains a relative unknown quantity and trip/ground will be fine.

RaceName: Sky Bet City Of York Stakes (Group 1)
Spotlight: Has some CV for one so lightly raced, having won the Group 2 Mill Reef (heavy) as a 2yo and added the Group 1 Champions Sprint at Ascot last October (good), beating previous Group 1 winner Lazzat; comeback run at the Curragh was a bit of a damp squib, though he was conceding weight all round in that Group 2 and he probably needed it; dangerous to dismiss, for all that he'll be into unknown territory inside today's final furlong.

RaceName: Sky Bet City Of York Stakes (Group 1)
Spotlight: Seriously progressive this season in 1m handicaps, including a near miss in the Lincoln (good to soft; won on soft) and victory in the Royal Hunt Cup at Royal Ascot (good to firm); dispelled any doubts about his Group-race credentials when emerging from last in a steadily run race to push Lake Forest to a neck in the 7f Lennox at Glorious Goodwood (good); that effort deserves an upgrade, so he's in the mix.

RaceName: Sky Bet City Of York Stakes (Group 1)
Spotlight: Japanese raider who has made his name over 6f, winning two Grade 1s on home soil and placed in three British Group 1s, latterly the July Cup at Newmarket where he wasn't stopping at the finish; ran well on his only start over 7f (in 2024) and it was over 1m that he won his first ever race; an intriguing runner, though the glaring concern is that his peak efforts have come on good or faster ground and this surface is likely to be the softest he's raced on (effective on yielding back home).

RaceName: Sky Bet City Of York Stakes (Group 1)
Spotlight: Prior to this year all his best form was at 7f on ground good or slower, and yet he popped up at 50-1 in a fast-ground Queen Anne and proved that was no flash in the pan with his close fourth to Bow Echo in the Sussex Stakes (again 1m on good to firm), in which he was nearest at the finish having been held up out the back; hard to knock.

RaceName: Sky Bet City Of York Stakes (Group 1)
Spotlight: A standing dish in Group races over 6f but had long given the impression that 7f might suit and she duly saw that trip out well to take the Group 3 Oak Tree at Glorious Goodwood (good to firm; could be even better on softer); the close proximity of the third/fourth horses would suggest that a repeat performance won't get the job done here, but she's a likeable mare who should give her running, especially with form figures of 121 on her last three visits to York; respected.

RaceName: Sky Bet City Of York Stakes (Group 1)
Spotlight: All runs at 6f on good or faster ground; unbeaten as a 2yo, winning a weak Gimcrack here 12 months ago on his second start (good to firm); lots to like about his comeback run at Chester, as he did a lot of early running from a bad draw and was picked off only late on; however, that was a Listed race and this is a new trip, so it looks a big ask.

RaceName: Sky Bet City Of York Stakes (Group 1)
Spotlight: Debut winner at two on soft and later beat this year's 1,000 Guineas heroine True Love in the Group 1 Phoenix Stakes (6f, good); no more than minor roles in three 1m Group 1s this season before justifying favouritism when his sights were lowered in a Curragh Group 2 last month (7f, good to firm); he didn't exactly blow his rivals away that day and he's probably playing for the places, for all that a fast-run race at 7f might be his ideal scenario these days.

RaceName: Sky Bet City Of York Stakes (Group 1)
OwnerName: Mrs John Magnier & Michael Tabor & Derrick Smith
Spotlight: Last two efforts in fast-ground Group 1s at 1m don't reflect his true ability and on going slower than good he has form figures of 114 (all on very soft) in Group 1s at 7f and 1m, with the defeat highly respectable on this season's reappearance when close up behind last weekend's Jacques le Marois winner Rayif; one to be interested in with cheekpieces given a go.

RaceName: Sky Bet City Of York Stakes (Group 1)
Spotlight: One of the best 2yos around last season, with his head defeat of Gstaad in the Group 1 National Stakes at the Curragh (7f, yielding; unraced on softer) his most striking piece of form; a setback ruled out him out of the 2,000 Guineas after shaping encouragingly in a trial, and he got messed about at a crucial stage when fifth in the Sussex (one place behind Ten Bob Tony); this shorter trip might be a better fit for him and, as he still retains some upside, he looks a key player.

RaceName: Philip Wilson Memorial Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Hat-trick (2m-extended 2m3f) before the break included two C&D wins in July, latest when scoring convincingly off an 8lb lower mark and the runner-up has run well since; this mark demands more but he's thriving and a bold bid can be expected for the four-timer.

RaceName: Philip Wilson Memorial Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
Spotlight: C&D winner in May and respectable second over hurdles the following month, but he was well beaten back over fences at Hexham (raced freely) last month and subsequently left Dan Skelton's stable for £5,000; retains chase potential but others are more persuasive.

RaceName: Philip Wilson Memorial Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Showed the benefit of wind surgery when winning three hurdle races on the bounce in May and very nearly defied a 4lb lower mark than this at Uttoxeter (2m4f, good) in July on chase debut; latest race was voided well before the finish; strong claims.

RaceName: Philip Wilson Memorial Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Useful hurdler in his prime but he's been well below that level in three starts for this stable since returning from a long absence, latest when a 34l fourth back over fences at Stratford (extended 2m3f) last month; has enough to prove at present.

RaceName: Tote Guarantee, Never Beaten By SP Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Three wins over hurdles including a Pertemps Qualifier at Leopardstown last year; fine fourth in a very competitive handicap hurdle at Punchestown; unseated early on his chase debut at Wexford last month; obvious claims on his return to hurdles.

RaceName: Tote Guarantee, Never Beaten By SP Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: First and second in the last two runnings of the Grand Annual at Cheltenham; slightly unlucky in a valuable handicap hurdle at Aintree when last seen; still potentially well handicapped over hurdles and should be a leading player; has won over 2m5f over fences.

RaceName: Tote Guarantee, Never Beaten By SP Handicap Hurdle
OwnerName: Eamon Leahy & Seamus O'Riordan & Edward Hayes
Spotlight: Five hurdle wins to her credit, including this race last year; not seen since running respectably behind Duke Silver at Leopardstown in December; 10lb higher than last year with an eight month absence to overcome.

RaceName: Tote Guarantee, Never Beaten By SP Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Five-time winner but quite lightly raced in recent times over hurdles and fences; mid-division over C&D in July and his forays over this sort of trip have not convinced; others preferred.

RaceName: Tote Guarantee, Never Beaten By SP Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Sligo maiden hurdle winner for Willie Mullins two years ago; three runs on the Flat for this stable have not revealed a huge amount; best watched.

RaceName: Tote Guarantee, Never Beaten By SP Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Very solid dual purpose performer; campaigned on the Flat and over fences this year, winning the Cork Derby and second in a Kilbeggan beginners chase; reverts back to hurdles with the stable in cracking form and makes obvious appeal.

RaceName: Tote Guarantee, Never Beaten By SP Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Point winner and progressive in three runs over hurdles, bolting up in a 3m maiden hurdle at Cork in January when last seen; Darragh O'Keeffe sticks with him and a very interesting handicap debutant despite almost eight months off.

RaceName: Tote Guarantee, Never Beaten By SP Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Second in a Galway beginners chase last year and a couple of decent efforts since; some encouragement from his effort at Galway last time but more needed.

RaceName: Tote Guarantee, Never Beaten By SP Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Dual winner over hurdles; not beaten far when stepped up to this trip in a handicap hurdle here last month; worth another try but others make more appeal

RaceName: Tote Guarantee, Never Beaten By SP Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Bumper and maiden hurdle winner for Gordon Elliott; two runs for his current stable and probably failed to see out the 3m2f at Ballinrobe last time; others preferred.

RaceName: Tote Guarantee, Never Beaten By SP Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Won over hurdles and fences in Britain on soft/heavy; standout effort for current yard came over here last month when coming home strongly to be beaten a nose in 2m5f handicap hurdle, after being a bit short of room and having to be switched in closing stages; up 3lb for that but should go well.

RaceName: Tote Guarantee, Never Beaten By SP Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Listowel maiden hurdle for Willie Mullins; much better effort at Galway last time on his second run for the stable; more needed again but not impossible to see him involved.

RaceName: Tote Guarantee, Never Beaten By SP Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Had a couple of these behind when a close second in a C&D handicap in July; failed to see out his race at Galway since but certainly respected on that previous course form.

RaceName: Tote Guarantee, Never Beaten By SP Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Got a 9lb hike for winning a Tramore maiden hurdle in May; well held in three novice hurdles since; 4lb wrong on his handicap debut and probably safe to look elsewhere.

RaceName: Powells Jewellery EBF Fillies' Conditions Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Down the field in the Albany Stakes at Royal Ascot but that is sandwiched by 6f wins at Nottingham (good) and Wolverhampton (AW); slower ground to contend with today but this Cheveley Park entrant is well drawn and shouldn't be far away if handling it.

RaceName: Powells Jewellery EBF Fillies' Conditions Stakes (GBB Race)
OwnerName: Exors Of The Late Sheikh Mohammed Obaid
Spotlight: Two runs at York, showing better form on the second occasion when missing out by a short-head four weeks ago (6f, good to firm; solid form); remains capable of better and she looks set for a big run.

RaceName: Powells Jewellery EBF Fillies' Conditions Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Her best run came at Chester (5.5f, good) but she looks exposed now and others bring much more compelling claims.

RaceName: Powells Jewellery EBF Fillies' Conditions Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Promising second behind a smart 2yo at Goodwood on debut; struggled at Royal Ascot before a bloodless success at Beverley (5f, good to firm); not at her best in a French Listed race two weeks ago; steps up to 6f for the first time; has the form to feature.

RaceName: Powells Jewellery EBF Fillies' Conditions Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Second on debut and put that experience to good use when comfortably seeing off four rivals at Hamilton (6f, good to firm) last month; didn't get home over 7f in a French Group 3 three weeks ago; has the inside stall and she holds solid claims back down in trip and class.

RaceName: Powells Jewellery EBF Fillies' Conditions Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Ran green when coming off the bridle on her debut at Newbury (6f, good to firm) five weeks ago; open to improvement but she has a useful standard to aim at in this field.

RaceName: Powells Jewellery EBF Fillies' Conditions Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Her Listed third at Newmarket (6f, good to firm) is head and shoulders above her other four runs; drawn widest and may prove vulnerable to less-exposed rivals.

RaceName: Hopeful Stakes (Sponsored By Blackwell Earthmoving) (Listed Race)
Spotlight: Kept on for Listed third at Doncaster (6f, good to soft) in March and was denied clear run when respectable sixth in Newcastle handicap (6f, AW) on latest outing in June but appears to face a tough assignment here.

RaceName: Hopeful Stakes (Sponsored By Blackwell Earthmoving) (Listed Race)
Spotlight: Led close home to win valuable 5f Ascot handicap in July and wasn't beaten far when back over 6f for Stewards' Cup at Glorious Goodwood (also good to firm) at start of this month; didn't fire at York (5.3f, good) on Wednesday, though, and needs a personal best here.

RaceName: Hopeful Stakes (Sponsored By Blackwell Earthmoving) (Listed Race)
Spotlight: Low-mileage 4yo who finished close up in valuable 7f handicaps at Royal Ascot and here (both good to firm) on last two appearances; doesn't have that much to find with the principals on this return to Listed company but has never run in a sprint before.

RaceName: Hopeful Stakes (Sponsored By Blackwell Earthmoving) (Listed Race)
Spotlight: Yet to win this season but took his form to a new level when fitted with blinkers for last two runs, looking unlucky not to finish closer than sixth in C&D Group 1 July Cup before running on well for second in 7f Newbury Group 2 (also good to firm) last Saturday; eased in grade today; the one to beat.

RaceName: Hopeful Stakes (Sponsored By Blackwell Earthmoving) (Listed Race)
Spotlight: 12-time winner, including 2024 edition of this race; has a bit to prove after two down-the-field finishes but faced tough task in Group 1 July Cup here last time and he looked as good as ever when creditable third in Group 3 on Rowley Mile here (6f, good) in April; in the shake-up if back on song.

RaceName: Hopeful Stakes (Sponsored By Blackwell Earthmoving) (Listed Race)
Spotlight: Won 6f Group 2 as a 2yo (good to soft) and scored in this grade at Sandown (5f, good) in June, after a break; carries 3lb penalty in stronger race today but could still have untapped potential back over this longer trip; shortlisted.

RaceName: Hopeful Stakes (Sponsored By Blackwell Earthmoving) (Listed Race)
Spotlight: Belied 66-1 odds when close second in Ascot Group 3 (6f, good to firm) on seasonal debut in May and subsequent Group 1 defeat over that C&D at Royal meeting is not viewed too harshly; may yet have a bigger run in her but others in this field have more convincing profiles.

RaceName: Coolmore Stud City Of Troy Tom Cooper Irish EBF Futurity Stakes (Group 2)
Spotlight: Mehmas colt made a winning start at Killarney last month (1m, good, Green Dreamer fifth); did well to finish a 0.75l second in Gowran Listed event latest after racing keenly; will need to settle better upped in class and dropped in trip.

RaceName: Coolmore Stud City Of Troy Tom Cooper Irish EBF Futurity Stakes (Group 2)
Spotlight: Mehmas colt is the most experienced in field with four runs; career best on latest when landing the 7f Group 3 Tyros Stakes at Leopardstown; the runner up Folsom Blues finished second behind Sun Goddess in the Group 1 Phoenix Stakes on his next start; leading form claims but looks the yard's second string on rider arrangements.

RaceName: Coolmore Stud City Of Troy Tom Cooper Irish EBF Futurity Stakes (Group 2)
Spotlight: Frankel colt was beaten at short odds over C&D (gd-yld) on debut in June but left that behind to win easily on quicker ground in a C&D maiden later that month, after which he was made favourite for the 2027 Epsom Derby; given a break since and he looks the yard's main hope on rider arrangements; likely to be thereabouts on first try in pattern company.

RaceName: Coolmore Stud City Of Troy Tom Cooper Irish EBF Futurity Stakes (Group 2)
Spotlight: Churchill colt was no match for City Of Dubai on debut at Killarney (1m, good); made all on second start in a 1m Leopardstown maiden (good) last month and the 2l runner up won a maiden next time out; should have enough pace for this shorter trip but Browne McMonagle prefers the chances of Nail House.

RaceName: Coolmore Stud City Of Troy Tom Cooper Irish EBF Futurity Stakes (Group 2)
Spotlight: No Nay Never colt landed 6f Fairyhouse maiden on debut (good); ran better than the bare result when a 4.75l fourth behind Florida Bay in the 7f Tyros Stakes at Leopardstown, denied a clear run at a crucial time; preferred by Browne McMonagle and could get closer to Florida Bay with a smoother passage.

RaceName: Coolmore Stud City Of Troy Tom Cooper Irish EBF Futurity Stakes (Group 2)
Spotlight: Justify colt beat subsequent Windsor Castle winner King Of Cloughan on debut at Leopardstown (7f, good) in May; made it 2-2 when landing the Listed Chesham Stakes at Royal Ascot in June (7f, gd-fm); given a two month break after that win; another big run likely on the cards.

RaceName: Sky Bet Ebor Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: 2m Group 1 entry; lightly raced 4yo, unraced on softer than good except on debut; has flourished this term, winning in some style at Carlisle (1m3f) in May and Royal Ascot (1m4f; 10lb higher today) in June; backed up the latter form when second in a steadily run Group 3 at Goodwood and looks well worth a crack at 1m6f.

RaceName: Sky Bet Ebor Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Not proven on worse than good to soft; fourth in this race in 2024; 7yo who is 0-13 since winning at Meydan in January 2025; has run really well in plenty of Group races in the interim, including the last two runnings of the Yorkshire Cup over C&D, but he ran a stinker in C&D Listed event in June and also disappointed here on latest start; big questions to answer after that.

RaceName: Sky Bet Ebor Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Probably acts on good to soft, much more to prove on soft; reliable 7yo who's never been better than this season (1m2f-2m); also seems to have found his limits but perhaps a handicap such as this will suit him better than the much smaller-field Group/Listed race's he's contested on last three starts.

RaceName: Sky Bet Ebor Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Seemed to be going places when he won a Group 3 at Newbury (1m5f, good to firm) last August, followed by a respectable sixth on soft ground in the St Leger, but he's been disappointing this term; headgear goes on.

RaceName: Sky Bet Ebor Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
OwnerName: Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed Al Maktoum
Spotlight: Won at Leicester (1m4f, good to soft) last October and reappeared with a good second at Goodwood (1m6f, good) in May, both from the front; soft ground was likely to blame at Epsom on Derby Day but recent return to action was pretty spectacular when a change in tactics saw him come from last to first in a well-contested 13-runner race at Southwell (1m3f, AW); has a 4lb penalty after that narrow win but this lightly raced 4yo now promises better still and a good 5lb claimer is enlisted; player if the ground isn't too soft.

RaceName: Sky Bet Ebor Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Won the Melrose on this card last year before a creditable last of seven in the soft-ground St Leger (sole run on softer than good); returned to a handicap off this mark at Glorious Goodwood (again 1m6f on good to firm) three weeks ago for a good fourth of 13 to Hopewell Rock, challenging smoothly over 2f out; that was after 11 weeks off and much more encouraging again.

RaceName: Sky Bet Ebor Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: 2m Group 1 entry with no ground worries; 1m2f Listed and Group 3 winner in Germany and last year he scored over 1m4f in France; sole Flat run for new connections was a good one when third in the 2m5f Queen Alexandra at Royal Ascot, travelling well turning for home; followed that by knuckling down well for a maiden hurdle win at the Galway festival and his trainer has won two of the last three Ebors, but a 7lb rise since Royal Ascot isn't ideal.

RaceName: Sky Bet Ebor Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: 2m Group 1 entry for Ascot in October, along with several others in this; unraced on good to soft and below form in a soft-ground run last term; unbeaten in 2026, having led in the closing stages on good to firm at the Newmarket Guineas meeting (1m4f) and Royal Ascot (1m6f; by a head); raised another 5lb but progressive and plenty to like if the ground proves suitable.

RaceName: Sky Bet Ebor Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Won on heavy as 2yo, unraced on soft; regular progress/promise (including on good to soft) in his first six handicaps, without winning; raced freely early on in the last of those when running out of steam at Royal Ascot (1m4f) but he then got his act together at Glorious Goodwood (upped to 1m6f, good to firm) three weeks ago when travelling smoothly in mid-division and going on over 1f out, before holding a hampered runner-up (who won well here on Wednesday); well treated under 4lb penalty.

RaceName: Sky Bet Ebor Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Close second in 1m7f French Group 2 (on very soft) last October remains his best form; he has a competitive handicap mark, though, as he showed when running on well from off the pace to be fourth of 17 to Opportunity at Royal Ascot (1m4f) last time; Ryan Moore stays on board; Irish St Leger entry with strong claims back up in trip.

RaceName: Sky Bet Ebor Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Markedly improved last year and even better this term, all on good or good to firm, although he had lots of soft-ground form in previous seasons; wore cheekpieces when staying-on third of 16 to Daiquiri Bay at Royal Ascot (1m6f) and close second at Newmarket (1m4f) 18 days later; raised another 3lb but each-way player if the ground is okay for him.

RaceName: Sky Bet Ebor Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Registered his highest rating in 1m6f Listed race on soft ground last April (his only time front-running); always prominent when strong finish took him to a handicap win at the Curragh (1m6f, yielding) this term and, although he wasn't discredited over 2m later in June, this trip on softer than good may well be the best fit; wears headgear for the first time.

RaceName: Sky Bet Ebor Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Not often seen on softer than good but he won on good to soft in June 2024; failed to shine at this meeting in 2024 or 2025, during a long losing run; he's broken that with two 2m wins on the AW this year, most notably in the Northumberland Plate at Newcastle in June, and also second at Newmarket (1m6f, good to firm) in May, but only mid-division behind Hopewell Rock at Goodwood three weeks ago; others seem more likely.

RaceName: Sky Bet Ebor Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: 2023 Royal Ascot winner who has also tasted the high life in top hurdle races; one of the market leaders in this in 2024 but came 12th; his attentions have been focused on the Flat this year but he hasn't been in peak form, 11th off this reduced mark behind Hopewell Rock last time; there's a chance that return to softer ground today will help; something needs to.

RaceName: Sky Bet Ebor Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Acts on good to soft but soft would be a worry; tricky to settle and is held up in rear; won the Cesarewitch at Newmarket (2m2f; 10lb higher today) last October and he's looked just as good on most starts since, without winning but late traffic woes seemingly prevented him from going close last time; without his usual jockey Billy Loughnane today but he was a close second last term under Clifford Lee; probably involved if he can get the breaks.

RaceName: Sky Bet Ebor Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Probably no ground worries; not a prolific winner, with his waiting tactics, but he was fourth in the Ebor last year off a 2lb higher mark; ran creditably on reappearance, before none of his three starts since panned out favourably; can be given a place chance.

RaceName: Sky Bet Ebor Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Just six races; came from the back when second on handicap debut at Haydock (1m6f, good to soft) last September and again when eventually well on top at York (1m4f, good; 8lb higher today) this May; the latter promised much, which was singularly unfulfilled when hot favourite at Newmarket (1m4f, good to firm) seven weeks ago; virtually first off the bridle that day but a return to 1m6f on softer ground today ensures that he remains of major interest.

RaceName: Sky Bet Ebor Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Unraced on the soft on Flat for nearly two years; progressive last season, most notably on good to firm with his win at Royal Ascot (2m4f) and second in this race; failed to shine at Ascot on first two starts this season (every chance over 1f out at the Royal meeting) before never dangerous when 40-1 in a recent Leopardstown Group 3; off the same mark as 12 months ago, however, this Irish St Leger entry could be dangerous to dismiss.

RaceName: Sky Bet Ebor Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: 4yo with just five races under his belt but he has 2m Group 1 entry for Ascot in October; won handicap debut at Hamilton (1m5f, good) in May and firmly in charge from over 1f out in 12-runner race at Ayr (1m5f, soft; always prominent) in June; up another 6lb today, inexperienced and drawn almost widest of all, but he strides out as if 1m6f will suit him well and has significantly more to give.

RaceName: Sky Bet Ebor Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Rarely seen on softer than good but it used to be okay (2023); made the frame only once (Saudi Arabia in February) from seven starts this year; admittedly hampered at Newmarket six weeks ago on latest outing, a race in which he ran well last term before finishing fifth in this; 7lb lower than 12 months ago and has a place squeak but there's been no win for over three years.

RaceName: Sky Bet Ebor Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Ran creditably twice over 1m6f last autumn, including on good to soft; this campaign is not that hard to forgive - over 1m2f/1m on first two occasions and with 2m for the Northumberland Plate (just 8-1) perhaps a stretch last time - although he has raced a bit freely; well treated judged on peak form and could be about to come good again.

RaceName: Sky Bet Ebor Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
OwnerName: H O S Syndicate & Oti Racing
Spotlight: Half-brother to 1m1f-1m2f winner Lord Charming (including Group 3; RPR 113); unraced until last September but won over 1m1f in Germany on first two starts and beaten 2l in a 1m2f Listed race at Chantilly (very soft) in October; 180,000euros buy last November and unraced since; it looked last time as if going beyond 1m2f would suit him well and this choice of engagement is highly respected for trainer who's won two of the last three Ebors.

RaceName: Torbay Weekly Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Three-time chase winner, latest at Stratford (extended 2m3f) in June, but 0-10 over hurdles; has left Shark Hanlon since a disappointing chase run at Uttoxeter last month but not out of this if reproducing his encouraging third off this mark at Market Rasen on penultimate start.

RaceName: Torbay Weekly Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Won at Exeter in October but has been poor since, including when pulled up and tailed off on two starts this summer; has become well treated and is capable if in the mood, but he's not without risk.

RaceName: Torbay Weekly Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Galway festival winner in 2024 but hasn't matched that level since and has been well beaten on four of his five starts for this yard this year, latest when a 16l fourth to Mi Sueno over C&D last month; remains with plenty to find with that rival despite better terms.

RaceName: Torbay Weekly Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Reverts to hurdles after an unsuccessful spell over fences; sole win came in this sphere nearly two years ago, albeit having been lightly campaigned since; now 3lb below that winning mark and the return to hurdles may see him in a better light.

RaceName: Torbay Weekly Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Bumper winner in July 2025 but his efforts over hurdles have been underwhelming, including in three handicaps; needs to recapture his earlier promise for Robert Stephens but a change of scenery may help as he makes his debut for Henrietta Knight with Sean Bowen booked.

RaceName: Torbay Weekly Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Below his best in three runs since returning from a break but he is on a competitive mark and may benefit from recent wind surgery.

RaceName: Torbay Weekly Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Off the mark at the 25th attempt when scoring comfortably over C&D in July and both subsequent efforts in defeat have been solid, including when a 5l third to Mi Sueno here last time; likely to be thereabouts again.

RaceName: Torbay Weekly Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: 16-race maiden and not easy to predict but went close over C&D in June before finishing 54l behind Mi Sueno back here next time; needs the first-time blinkers to prove a positive addition.

RaceName: Torbay Weekly Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Dual Flat winner who has produced two encouraging placed efforts over C&D of late; has a bit to find with some of these but should be thereabouts.

RaceName: Torbay Weekly Handicap Hurdle
Spotlight: Returned to form with a C&D win on last month's debut for Nick Scholfield, having a few of these in behind and scoring a shade cosily; remains well treated despite a 5lb rise and is the one to beat if backing up that effort.

RaceName: Moynihan Scaffolding Ltd. And The Warehouse Cafe Beginners Chase
Spotlight: Very five-time winning useful hurdler, rated 147, goes on any ground; ran to form when 3l second on chase debut at Galway (2m2f, good) 25 days ago; was well held by Daddy Long Legs over hurdles at Limerick in July but was off a break and now has the benefit of a chase run under his belt; big chance.

RaceName: Moynihan Scaffolding Ltd. And The Warehouse Cafe Beginners Chase
Spotlight: Five-time winning hurdler, including Grade 3, rated 149 in that sphere; latest success in Ballinrobe (2m2f, good) conditions hurdle in May; solid three runs, including second over hurdles at Limerick since; should go close on chase debut.

RaceName: Moynihan Scaffolding Ltd. And The Warehouse Cafe Beginners Chase
Spotlight: Largely consistent hurdler, latest win came at Limerick (16.5f, good) in handicap off 102, bolted up by 15l; couldn't land a blow off 12lb higher lto; plenty on plate on chase debut; cheekpieces tried.

RaceName: Moynihan Scaffolding Ltd. And The Warehouse Cafe Beginners Chase
Spotlight: Some good placed efforts in maiden hurdles before getting off the mark at Navan (2m, soft) in March; unseated at second on chase debut 107 days ago; this a tough ask against some smart hurdlers but he's unexposed and can feature.

RaceName: Moynihan Scaffolding Ltd. And The Warehouse Cafe Beginners Chase
Spotlight: Gained fourth hurdles success with 3.25l victory in Galway Hurdle (2m, good) off 129 23 days ago; still has a bit to find with Daddy Long Legs and Bowensonfire on ratings but claims if taking to new discipline.

RaceName: Moynihan Scaffolding Ltd. And The Warehouse Cafe Beginners Chase
Spotlight: Consistent 103-rated handicapper over hurdles and fences; pulled up on last chase start in June; outsider.

RaceName: British Stallion Stud EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: First foal; dam unraced sister to winners Al Hamdany (useful 1m-1m4f including 2yo/KSA) and Schwartz (1m5f-2m), half-sister to winners Indigo Times (1m5f-2m) and Fox Kasper (8.7f-11.5f); drawn widest on debut and perhaps best watched.

RaceName: British Stallion Stud EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Made a low-key debut for Gemma Tutty at Musselburgh (5f, good) in June; withdrawn having played up at the start at Ayr this month (300-1 at the time of withdrawal); no appeal.

RaceName: British Stallion Stud EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Finished last of eight at Sandown (5f, good to firm) on her debut four weeks ago but she was sent off favourite; bred to do much better and that initial experience won't have been lost on her.

RaceName: British Stallion Stud EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 700,000gns yearling; second foal of a French Group-placed 5f 2yo winner (RPR 98), herself a half-sister to French winners Allure (1m7f) and Aniyla (1m1f); holds a Cheveley Park entry; makes her debut in a winnable race and she is of obvious interest.

RaceName: British Stallion Stud EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Modest RPRs in two 6f fillies' maidens this summer; should be quick enough for the drop in trip but she will need to improve for it.

RaceName: British Stallion Stud EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Down the field in two 6f runs this summer (tongue tied latest, absent today); drops to 5f with a point to prove.

RaceName: £200,000 Tattersalls Somerville Auction Stakes (GBB Race)
OwnerName: A Bit On The Side & Partner
Spotlight: Yet to add to debut win in March and was below form on latest outing but wasn't beaten far when sixth in Windsor Castle at Royal Ascot (6f, good to firm), and subsequently went close in a 5f Sandown Listed race (good); each-way claims at least if back on song.

RaceName: £200,000 Tattersalls Somerville Auction Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Began career with two 6f wins and has performed admirably well in two subsequent 6f Group 2s, finishing fifth in Coventry at Royal Ascot and third in Richmond at Glorious Goodwood; the class act in this line-up.

RaceName: £200,000 Tattersalls Somerville Auction Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Shaped with promise on last month's debut at Newbury and was too good for useful rival in three-runner contest at Nottingham (also 6f, good to firm) 11 days ago; this is tougher but he's well bred and remains unexposed.

RaceName: £200,000 Tattersalls Somerville Auction Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Bettered low-key debut and was only beaten about 2l when fifth of eight in Pontefract maiden (6f, good to firm) this month but needs to take another big step forward here.

RaceName: £200,000 Tattersalls Somerville Auction Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Creditable third at York in June and battled well to pip odds-on newcomer in four-runner Ayr maiden (also 6f, good) last month; might still have more to offer but is not really favoured by these terms.

RaceName: £200,000 Tattersalls Somerville Auction Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Won two quite valuable sellers (both 6f, good) this spring and looked unlucky when very close second in recent Windsor nursery (6f, good to firm); more exposed than most of these but ought to give another good account.

RaceName: £200,000 Tattersalls Somerville Auction Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Shaped well when second on debut at Thirsk (5f, good) three weeks ago, form that was given good boost when winner came second in big-field sales race at York on Thursday; needs improvement here but has the potential.

RaceName: £200,000 Tattersalls Somerville Auction Stakes (GBB Race)
